author: AntD1975
text:
Labour are robbing us blind!!!

The claim that David Lammy, as Foreign Secretary, has incurred £521,525 in food and drink expenses over 233 days, averaging £2,238 per day, is based on recent reports. According to The Times, the Foreign Office spent £521,525 on "restaurants and bars" during the first four months of the Labour government.  However, it's important to note that this figure represents the total expenditure of the entire department, not solely David Lammy's personal expenses.

Regarding the state pension, the full new State Pension rate is £221.20 per week as of the 2024-2025 financial year.  This equates to approximately £31.60 per day.

In summary, while the reported departmental expenditure on food and drink averages around £2,238 per day, this is a collective figure for the Foreign Office and not individual spending by David Lammy. The comparison to the daily state pension amount of £31.60 highlights a significant disparity between government departmental spending and individual pension income.

author: truthrising1
text:
Keir Starmer, ringmaster extraordinaire, tap-danced into Number 10 on a glittering tightrope of lies so absurd they’d make a circus clown blush. He unveiled ‘Rachael from accounts,’ his imaginary bookkeeper,a budget fairy straight out of a pantomime, whimpering about a £22 billion black hole that vanished in a puff of smoke the moment the OBR flicked on the lights and revealed it as the flimsiest plot twist since Cinderella’s tax return. Enter Jonathan Reynolds, Labour’s  Business Secretary, who twirled onto the stage boasting solicitor credentials—only to trip over his own fibs, unmasked as a mere trainee with a flair for fiction, winking at Starmer as if it’s all part of the act. Winter Fuel Payments? Poof!—snatched from 10 million pensioners with a magician’s flourish, all to plug a deficit as real as a unicorn’s overdraft. Taxes? Up £40 billion in a Budget so cartoonishly cruel it’s like Wile E. Coyote wrote it—National Insurance smacks employers, inheritance tax squashes farmers, and VAT on school fees kicks parents square in the shins—every promise to ‘protect the little guy’ tossed into the woodchipper with a villainous cackle.

But step right up folks, the freak show’s just warming up! Small boats? Over 30,000 illegals waltz across the Channel in 2024, thumbing their noses at Starmer’s £75 million ‘smash the gangs’ flop—less a policy, more a punchline. Foreign criminals? Our star attractions!—26,000 loaf about, racking up 10,000 crimes a year; one Albanian tough guy sobs he’ll miss his chicken nuggets too much to leave, rapists coo the British drizzle suits, and a Jamaican machete maestro pirouettes past deportation with a ‘human rights’ encore— Treated to a £450 million goodie bag—PlayStations, cinema, gym memberships, and a fresh trim—because nothing screams ‘integration’ like a taxpayer-funded Netflix binge, while £7 million keeps them in plush hotels and £135 million dribbles to Rwanda for a scheme Starmer canned but still bankrolls like a drunk uncle at a slot machine. The NHS? tragic sideshow—7.6 million queue in the rain, no scanners, no fixes, just Starmer crooning lullabies from the big top. Free speech? Sawn in half by the Online Safety Act, while a judiciary—more like Starmer’s obedient poodle than justice’s watchdog—chucking Stephen Dixon in the clink for two years over a Facebook quip, while tax crime soars £13 billion a year, untaxed and untouchable. Farmers? Fleeced by 20% legacy taxes—roll up, see the rural ruin! Prisons? 1,700 hoodlums, including slashers, tumble out early because Starmer miscounted. The two-child cap? A cruel trap, locking 4.33 million kids in poverty while his MPs juggle excuses. Chagos? Handed to Mauritius with an £18 billion bow—ta-da! 

Tulip Siddiq? Our tightrope walker, teetering in a £4 billion Bangladesh scandal—Starmer’s starlet now a pratfall. Andrew Gwynne? Fired for WhatsApp venom—cursing pensioners and smearing Jews—yet Starmer let him fester like a bad juggler till the boos rang out. Benefit fraud? £35 billion vanishes to crime gangs while Liz Kendall naps through the heist. The economy? A collapsing big top—Reeves bows to Beijing, peddling Britain’s soul as bonds plummet and her fiscal rules snap like cheap trapeze wires.

And now, the grand finale—David Lammy, reparations ringmaster, pirouetting globally in a top hat, itching to shovel billions to any nation with a sob story and a colonial coupon, while 4.33 million British kids go hungry and pensioners turn blue. Ukraine? £15 billion tossed into the hat—£3 billion yearly ‘for as long as it takes, while Britain’s needy get a stale crust. Cue £14 billion for foreign aid, £11.6 billion for climate selfies, £84 million to Africa, £12 million to Mauritius—a global giveaway extravaganza, hogwash with every flung coin. The disabled and vulnerable? 1.6 million on PIP, trembling as Starmer threatens their crumbs to flex his ‘tough guy’ act .

This isn’t governance, it’s a grotesque cabaret .
